meta.title: Career — Patrick Brant
meta.description: From inorganic chemistry at Arizona and Purdue to thirty-seven years at ExxonMobil Chemical, and an independent practice in polyolefins since 2019.

sections.label: Career
sections.quote: From inorganic chemistry <t>to the reactor floor.</t>
sections.sub: Arizona, Purdue and the Naval Research Laboratory; then thirty-seven years at ExxonMobil Chemical; then a practice of his own.

sections.label: ExxonMobil Chemical
sections.title: Thirty-seven years, <t>two chairs.</t>
sections.lede: Dates from his public profile; the work as described in his speaker biographies.

groups.label: Roles
names: Chief Polymer Science Advisor, ExxonMobil Chemical Company — June 2011 to December 2018, Houston and Baytown
Chief Scientist, Global R&D, ExxonMobil Chemical — April 2000 to June 2011: technical and organisation leadership
Research and leadership roles from 1981, Exxon Chemical Company, Baytown: input, guidance and stewardship of the polyolefins R&D portfolio; programme initiation, management and team leadership

groups.label: The work
names: Supported metallocene catalyst design, synthesis, characterisation and operation in gas-phase reactors: the research behind the commercialisation of metallocene polyethylenes
Structure–property relationships in the solid and melt state; polyolefin blends, including impact copolymers
Synthesis and functionalisation of new polyolefins, from laboratory to scale-up and commercialisation
Separator design and fabrication for lithium-ion batteries, from consumer electronics to transportation formats: the 2008 ICIS Innovation Award
Markets and applications: packaging, automotive, adhesives, engine-oil additives; plant and customer troubleshooting

groups.label: In public
names: More than 25 interviews with print and television media, a commercial, and ExxonMobil speaker at internal and external functions, 2006–2010
Invited speaker in academic and industrial formats; co-organiser of ISPAC 2015, Houston

sections.label: Timeline
sections.title: From George Mason, 1972, <t>to a practice of his own.</t>

groups.label: Practice
names: Consultant and Entrepreneur, self-employed — Houston, since January 2019
Expert witness in patent matters, occasional, since 2019
Founder, Molecular Joinery, LLC — Seabrook, Texas: composite and nanocomposite design, coupling-agent chemistry, coatings

groups.label: Research & programmes
names: Research collaborator, University of Houston — semi-crystalline polyolefins, with the Karim group
Research collaborator, Baylor University — Grubbs-catalysed ROMP for oil-field applications, with David Jack
Symposium Chair, Polymers: sustainability, processes, applications & characterization — TechConnect World, Austin, 2025
Speaker, Orphan & Idle Wells 2026 — plugging abandoned wells with ROMP chemistry

groups.label: Societies
names: American Chemical Society
American Physical Society
Society of Plastics Engineers

groups.label: Degrees and fellowships
names: Ph.D., Inorganic Chemistry — University of Arizona, 1972–1977
Post-doctoral research, inorganic and organometallic chemistry — Purdue University, 1977
National Research Council Fellowship — Naval Research Laboratory, Washington, D.C., 1978
B.Sc., Chemistry — George Mason University, 1972
